findings.fix: Add a `<caption>` such as "Current zone status."
findings.violation: The table has no `<caption>`, so it lacks an accessible name for screen-reader users browsing by table list.

findings.evidence: "Updates post to the schedule page within one business day." follows both "report a service issue by calling rider services" and "check real time arrivals at any station kiosk."

findings.fix: Clarify (or remove, if placeholder) what the control deletes, and implement it as a native `<button>` element.
findings.violation: A "Delete item" control appears with no explanation of what item it deletes, and it is built as a div with role="button" instead of a native `<button>`, risking missing default keyboard activation behavior.

findings.evidence: `<div class="wizard-steps">` containing plain `<div class="step">` elements: "Choose a plan," "Enter payment details," "Confirm your order"
findings.fix: Add introductory text, mark the steps up as an ordered list, and indicate the active step with `aria-current="step"`.
findings.violation: The wizard has no lead-in text explaining its purpose and no current-step indicator (no `aria-current`, no list semantics), so sighted and assistive-technology users alike can't tell which step is active or why it's there.

findings.evidence: `<label for="email" id="s3-form-email-label">Email address</label>` with no "(required)"/"(optional)" qualifier, unlike the phone label that follows
findings.fix: Add an explicit "(required)" or "(optional)" qualifier to the email label.

findings.evidence: `<label for="phone">Phone number (required)</label>` paired with `<input id="phone" type="tel">`
findings.violation: The label text says the field is required, but the input has no `required` or `aria-required="true"` attribute, so assistive technology and native form validation won't treat it as required.

findings.fix: Set `aria-invalid="false"` or omit it by default, applying "true" only after a failed validation.
findings.violation: `aria-invalid` is hardcoded to "true" in the static markup, so the field is announced as invalid before the user has entered anything or submitted the form.
